Agent: backend-core (Derek Olsen)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes (check-ins via GROK_TO_CLAUDE.md)
Kind: engine
Epic: E1 (docs/vendor/EPICS.md)
Target release: 0.4

Worktree: none until unblocked (then `.vendor-wt/wo-506` on `vendor/wo-506` from main)
Tracker: issue pending (in-house syncs freemyid-pm)
Order: start only after WO-503 is merged (they share a file or a behaviour this builds on); rebase on main first.

## Goal
One call that takes a path and a passphrase and returns a validated bundle document or a plain-language failure, so the CLI and the wizard do not each re-implement the order of checks. The decrypt step is passed in (`opener`) so this module never imports `crypto`.

## Blocked: what in-house must provide first
In-house must change `crypto.py` (`export_with_passphrase` / `import_with_passphrase`, `crypto.py:182-205`) so that (1) a wrong passphrase, a damaged file and "not a bundle" raise three distinct exception classes instead of one `ValueError` with a message (today `import_with_passphrase` collapses wrong-passphrase, truncation and tampering on purpose, `crypto.py:203-205`; in-house decides whether telling them apart is acceptable, and that is a security decision), (2) the header carries a one-byte format version (a `VP2` magic or a version byte) so scrypt cost can be raised later, and (3) a documented helper exists to estimate time cost so the UI can show "this takes a few seconds". Also in-house: the passphrase rules (minimum length, a generated word-list suggestion) belong in `crypto.py` or the wizard, not here. When that lands, Grok adds `open_bundle_file(path, passphrase, *, opener) -> OpenedBundle` to `setup_config.py`: size check, `peek_bundle_blob`, the injected opener, `validate_bundle_doc`, and a single `SetupFileError` with plain words per failure kind. No crypto code is written in this WO.

Not startable by a vendor. In-house unblocks it by changing the status line and posting a GO.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. With a fake `opener`, each failure kind (missing file, unreadable, header failure, wrong passphrase, damaged, invalid document) maps to its own plain message; none contains a path outside the file name, a value or a traceback.
2. The success path returns the document and the `BundleDocCheck` and never writes anything.
3. The file is read once, capped at `MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES + 1` bytes (same pattern as `monitor.load_previous`, `monitor.py:404-420`).
4. Windows paths with spaces and non-ASCII names work (`tmp_path`).
5. WO-501..503 tests pass unchanged.

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Tests pass on Windows too (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`). Check `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and the in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard.
